question: Should OpenClaw intentionally fail closed for existing byte-size config values outside JavaScript's safe-integer range in this PR?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and matches the dependency contract, but stricter config validation can change upgrade behavior for users who already have unsafe byte-size values.

options.title: Accept the narrow fail-closed repair
options.body: Treat unsafe byte counts as invalid config, remove the changelog hunk, and merge through the normal maintainer gate.

options.title: Add upgrade/doctor handling first
options.body: Require a diagnostic or doctor path for unsafe byte-size config values before the stricter validation lands.

options.title: Preserve compatibility by default
options.body: Keep existing rounding behavior unless maintainers want an explicit strict mode or broader config migration plan.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow fail-closed repair
recommendation.body: Treat unsafe byte counts as invalid config, remove the changelog hunk, and merge through the normal maintainer gate.
